newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Coca-Cola plans big investment in S.Africa.
newsitem.headline: Coca-Cola plans big investment in S.Africa.

text.p: U.S. soft drinks giant Coca-Cola Co said on Monday it was joining with its seven South African bottlers to invest 1.25 billion rand ($275 million) in South Africa over the next five years.

Coca-Cola Co president and chief operating officer Doug Ivester said the Atlanta-based company intended to double its business in South Africa as a result of the investment, which would be split on a 50-50 basis between Coca-Cola and its bottlers.
"We will be investing well in excess of one billion rand in South Africa over the next five years targeted at expanding and improving the availability of our product," Ivester told a news conference.

"We believe in the future of South Africa. We believe South Africa offers tremendous growth opportunities to those who show long-term discipline and we believe the time to invest in South Africa is now," he said.
The Coca-Cola announcement, which local analysts saw as a vote of confidence in South Africa, help boost the rand to its best levels in 3-1/2 months on Monday.
In afternoon trade it was quoted against the U.S. dollar at 4.5240/70 from 4.5635/65 at Friday's close.
"The country's dynamics are such that now this seems an appropriate time for this investment to take off," Ivester said.

The investment would be used primarily to buy coolers and other equipment as well as to improve support systems that Ivester said would significantly boost the availability of its product to capture South Africa's emerging urban consumers.

"This is not about bottling plants, it's about expanding the marketing infrastructure, this is about energising the market to increase demand and consumption," Coca-Cola Southern Africa president Charles Frenette said.
Frenette said the actual size of the investment per year would depend on the needs of the marketplace.
"Our objective is to increase the amount of soft drinks consumed in this country," Frenette said.
He and Ivester declined to say how much of a share of the South African market Coca-Cola has cornered over its rival Pepsico Inc, which re-entered the market two years ago.
"It's not something we discuss publicly. The market is big enough here that we can expand without taking market share from anybody," Ivester said.
In addition to Coca-Cola, the company markets Sprite, Fanta, Sparletta, Stoney and other soft drink brands throughout South Africa. The country is the company's 10th largest market worldwide.
Its drinks are bottled by seven South African-owned concerns -- Amalgamated Beverage Industries, Coca-Cola Bottlers Mpumalanga, Coca-Cola SABCO, Cooks, Kilimanjaro, Peninsula Beverages and Suncrush.
Ivester said Coca-Cola was also looking at expanding in the rest of Africa, adding announcements would be made in the appropriate countries. He is scheduled to visit Zimbabwe, Kenya and Tanzania.
